A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same HCFL/HCFL+ research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original federated-learning experiments on CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and Tiny-ImageNet, including component ablations, noisy-label experiments and ResNet18 results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds experiments on FedSoft-based variants, component effects, resource costs, heterogeneity and clustering quality.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 introduces HCFL+ (FedSoft), replacing HCFL+ (FedEM)'s local training with proximal-regularized updates, evaluated in Table 10. The original shared extractor, clustering objectives, weight updates and cluster adaptation components otherwise remain.

E1.justification: The datasets and classification tasks are retained, but Table 12 adds a stronger concept-shift condition beyond the earlier beta values of 0.2 and 0.4. Its exact severity is ambiguous: the caption states beta = 0.8 while the column heading states 0.9.

E2.justification: FedSoft, previously discussed but not experimentally compared, becomes an evaluated baseline in v2 Table 10. The comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce two- and four-class client partitions, rho = 0.01, memory and simulation-time measurements, and paired validation/test reporting at ICFL's selected rounds. The existing defaults of 100 clients, 200 communication rounds and one local epoch remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Table 3 tests very small rho, Table 9 examines ICFL's checkpoint-dependent trade-off, Table 10 adds the HCFL-prime component ablation, and Tables 11–13 examine efficiency, stronger heterogeneity and class-to-cluster assignments. Earlier component ablations and noisy-label tests are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly specifies averaging over three trials; v1 already reported plus/minus values but did not disclose the trial count. This is additional reporting, not evidence of increased runs. The new supplementary tables mostly provide point estimates without corresponding uncertainty information.

E6.justification: The original seven tables retain their numerical results, while v2 Tables 3 and 9–13 add substantial evidence on variants, trade-offs, efficiency and clustering. For example, Table 10 newly reports CIFAR10 test accuracy of 34.70 for FedSoft and 51.23 for HCFL+ (FedSoft); these are new comparisons, not improvements over v1 scores.

T1.justification: The assumptions, proofs and Theorem B.12 are retained. However, v2's abbreviated Eq. (4) loses the denominator likelihood's dependence on the summed cluster index, and Eq. (7) uses the old rather than updated predictor parameters. These limited changes are mathematically non-equivalent as printed and conflict with the unchanged Appendix A formulas.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly narrows the scope to supervised clustered FL and data heterogeneity, distinguishing unsupervised clustering and other privacy/communication techniques. The central claims about the four-tier framework, four HCFL+ enhancements and personalization–generalization benefits remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds discussion of severe sample imbalance hindering convergence, privacy-technique integration, and interpretations of the new diagnostics. Some interpretations overreach: Appendix E.3 claims superiority across all heterogeneous settings, although Table 12 reports four-class test accuracy of 62.30 for HCFL+ versus 72.30 for ICFL.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with a repository location. Appendix E.2 newly identifies NVIDIA RTX 3090 hardware, and Appendix E.3 supplies a parameter-count explanation for the extractor/classifier split. Existing learning-rate choices and training-budget disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Diao, Ding, Ma, Qiao and Reisser, including an explicit distinction from unsupervised federated clustering. Remark B.13 also positions the retained unequal-cluster-size analysis against earlier balanced-cluster studies. The overall related-work organization and positioning remain similar.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introductory motivation are edited, and an appendix roadmap is added. Prototype implementation details are repeated in the main text, while the main-text convergence theorem is replaced by an appendix reference. Most prose and the section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The ICLR formatting changes widths, typography and equation layout throughout. Six new tables are added, Table 1 gains fixed/adaptive-cluster grouping, and the cluster-count plot moves from main-text Figure 3 to appendix Figure 4. The existing ablation figure is retained as Figure 3.

improvement.justification: The added ablations and diagnostics improve the evidence about component effects, resource costs and trade-offs, while code-access, hardware and trial-count disclosures improve reproducibility information. The net gain is limited by new equation inconsistencies and Table 12's conflicting beta labels and overstated superiority claim. The original benchmark evidence and appendix proofs remain available.
